content.text:
Yes. IntelliJ is the Flathub Flatpak, and its sandbox can see `~/.local/share/mise/shims`, but each shim is a symlink to host `/usr/bin/mise`:

```text
~/.local/share/mise/shims/rustc -> /usr/bin/mise
```

Flatpak reserves its own `/usr`, so that target is unavailable inside the sandbox. The shim therefore appears broken.

Use the Rustup-backed binaries directly in IntelliJ instead:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cargo
```

(or `~/.cargo/bin/rustc` where a compiler path is requested). I verified those work inside the IntelliJ Flatpak and report Rust/Cargo `1.98.1`.

This is consistent with Mise currently managing Rust through the Rustup installation under `~/.cargo`; the version is current despite that directory name.
/home/alexis/.cargo/bin points to a toolchain version of 1.93.1 in Intellij

content.text:
You’re right—IntelliJ uses 1.93.1 because this project explicitly pins it in:

[`rust-toolchain.toml`](/home/alexis/Development/private/foglio/rust-toolchain.toml)

```toml
channel = "1.93.1"
```

`~/.cargo/bin/cargo` is Rustup’s proxy. Outside Mise activation, Rustup reads that project file and selects 1.93.1. Your shell gets 1.98.1 because Mise’s project config (`mise.toml`, `rust = "latest"`) overrides it via `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`.

To make IntelliJ use 1.98 too, update `rust-toolchain.toml` to:

```toml
channel = "1.98.1"
```

That is the robust fix; IntelliJ can then use `~/.cargo/bin/cargo` normally, without needing access to Mise shims.
